section_summary: This section consists of a confidential letter dated October 21, 1949, from John M. Allison, Director of the Office of Northeast Asian Affairs at the Department of State, to Robert R. West, Deputy to the Under Secretary of the Army. Allison discusses a draft policy proposal for the Far Eastern Commission regarding the progressive relaxation of SCAP control and the assumption of criminal and civil jurisdiction by Japanese courts over United Nations nationals, excluding official occupation personnel. The Department of State requests Army concurrence on the draft decision before initiating informal diplomatic consultations with the United Kingdom and France.

subfiles.about: A letter conveying the State Department's draft proposal to revise Far Eastern Commission policy on the exercise of criminal and civil jurisdiction by Japanese courts over United Nations nationals.
subfiles.from: John M. Allison, Director, Office of Northeast Asian Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: State concurs in principle with the Army on granting Japanese courts criminal and civil jurisdiction over non-occupation United Nations nationals under progressive SCAP relaxation, requesting Army concurrence before informal consultations with the United Kingdom and France.
